    55	### 1.2 The problems it answers
    56	
    57	Three things make an analyst's job hard, and the record is built against each:
    58	
    59	1. **Most of what arrives is noise; the increment is rare.** Alex: "不是什么事情都是惊弓之鸟需要抽取，杂音还是很大的，我们整体应该倾向谨慎…同时我们要敏感一些新的信息带来的增量不要错过" (D243).
    60	   The system keeps few statements and only big questions. Alex: "我觉得核心就是这个颗粒度的把控要符合一个高端的hedge fund analyst 的思维。不要搜集一堆鸡毛蒜皮的事情，要看重要的大事，合并整合关键的信息" (D248).
    61	2. **One statement arrives many times.** The same forecast comes through many outlets and reposts. Counted as many, it fakes
    62	   conviction. The record keeps it as one statement with all its sources (section 6).
    63	3. **An answer written from scratch has no memory and no score.** It cannot say what it concluded two weeks ago, what changed it, or
    64	   whether it was right. The record fixes the question and its answers first, dates every judgement with its evidence, and closes the
    65	   answer on the due day.
    66	
    67	**Why one model call over everything does not do this.** Alex, on asking a general model to research theses: "it's actually very, very
    68	hard because it hallucinates, it, you know, it doesn't really work" (2026-10-22). Two measurements point at what breaks:
    69	- **Too much material in one request fails.** In a three-month run the data-center revenue question held 1,768 linked pieces. Its
    70	  judging request was 292 KB with 698 evidence ids. The judge mislabelled ids, its answers were refused, and whole days halted (D358;
    71	  Alex: "bloating evidence 的问题 … 很严重，需要解决").
    72	- **The reasoning is not the bottleneck; delivering the right facts to the right question is.** The custom-chip question, sent as it
    73	  was, answered "below $40 billion" 9 times of 9. With the Broadcom and Trainium facts the ledger already held added, it left the
    74	  lowest range 9 times of 9 and reasoned as the expert readers did (`docs/prd/10-filing-phase.md`, Evidence).
    75	
    76	So the architecture puts its effort into reading, filing and grouping, and keeps the judge small and fixed. No test has compared the
    77	system with a single general-model call on the same questions; the case rests on the measurements above.

   190	## 3. The information the system works with
   191	
   192	| Information | What it is for |
   193	|---|---|
   194	| Incoming item | The article or other material Hummingbird supplies, with its source, speaker and publication information when known. |
   195	| Thesis | A big matter an analyst would follow for a company or a theme, written as a question with the outcome to track and its period when known. |
   196	| Evidence | A statement, number, event or view from an item that an analyst would note, with its source passages, speaker, original party, statement date and tier. It may link to one or more theses, or to none yet. |
   197	| Evidence group | One statement and every later report of it. Each report keeps its own text and source inside the group; the first record is never rewritten. |
   198	| Revision link | A later version of a statement (a revised forecast, an official denial of a report), linked to the earlier one; the earlier statement stays. |
   199	| Judged question | The one part of a thesis that is judged: an event (it happened, it is ruled out, or still open) or a figure (five ranges set against a reference, with the favourable end registered), with its due day. Other parts of the thesis are listed as not judged. |
   200	| Judgement | The current answer to a judged question, with the evidence it cites, written by the daily judge. |
   201	| Closing | The final answer recorded on the due day. |
   202	| Run trace | The item, everything the model was shown, its raw answer and the library before and after, kept for review. |
   203	
   204	A thesis can have many pieces of evidence. One statement can inform several theses and is stored once. An article can feed open theses,
   205	open a new one, add statements kept without links, or add nothing.

    84	  "the demand, supply, competition and pricing that make it more or less likely"; the total-revenue question taking more is an accepted cost, "bounded by
    85	  the narrowest-question rule and the driver questions"), D265 (code keeps only the narrowest), D273 (the fallback sentence), D355 (the two failed tests

    88	  for a bank, a drug maker, a retailer or a chip company, names neither NVIDIA nor its products or figures, and is not taken from a test article; a
    89	  classification is written as a closed set with two or three examples per class, replacing the abstract wording; quality is not fixed by lengthening
    90	  the prompt: remove as much as is added, or write down the reason.
    91	- **Code decides only "is it the same thing", never "does it matter"** (AGENTS §2).
    92	
    93	## 5. What to do
    94	
    95	Status: the links-rule version that carried items 1–3 (v74l) failed its one test (§8 step 5); D361 keeps the fallback sentence, so item 3 is not carried out. The plan below is kept as written.
    96	
    97	1. **Replace the abstract sentence "makes the answer more or less likely through demand, supply, competition or pricing" with the few classes in which an analyst recognises an indirect relation, written as a closed set, each class with two or three examples from other industries** (AGENTS §6: one
    98	   abstract sentence is a coin flip on every send; examples replace it). A first draft of the classes (checked against the standard line by line at
    99	   design time; it holds only meanings the standard already has):
   100	   - The question's own figure: this question's figures, guidance, estimates and revisions (estimates for another period or another population follow
   101	     the existing rule).
   102	   - The other side of the same money: a seller's revenue from the buyers the question counts; those buyers' orders and backlog with these sellers.
   103	   - Price and volume: a product's price or shipments, for the question on that product's revenue.
   104	   - Variants and parts: a product's variants, alternatives, key parts and schedule changes, for the question on that product's launch.
   105	   - Demand, supply and competition moves with a number: customers' orders and capital-spending plans, suppliers' capacity and prices, competitors'
   106	     sales and share, for the question they affect.
   107	2. **State how to file a fact when two specific questions both bear on it** (the problem the `definition_no_fallback` arm exposed: Morgan Stanley's rack
   108	   price was filed under the buyers' capital-spending question, and the seller's Rubin revenue question lost it). One home per fact (D207): file it under
   109	   the question its figure measures most directly (for example, a hotel's room rate goes under its room-revenue question, not under the
   110	   travellers'-spending question; a parts maker's revenue from carmakers goes under the carmakers' parts-spending question, not under a rival parts
   111	   maker's share question); when one sentence gives a separate figure for each of two questions, write two items, each filed under its own question
   112	   (code stores two items that quote the same sentence as one record linked to both questions); never also file it under a broader question about the
   113	   same company (the failure of D355's test 2: the model filed it under an NVIDIA revenue question as well). The original draft's "when the other
   114	   party's question is open … file it there as well" conflicted with D207 and was deleted on 2026-11-04 with Alex's agreement (D360).
   115	3. **Delete the fallback sentence** and return to the standard's §6: when no question takes a fact, it is not filed; code drops it as "no home" and
   116	   records it (D209), and evaluation reads each one.
   117	4. Change only the one place that holds the filing rule; report its length in characters before and after, and write down the reason for any growth
   118	   (this time's reason: examples replace one abstract sentence).
   119	
   120	## 6. How to measure (the ruler does not move; the method does not change again)
   121	
   122	- **Requests**: rebuild each stored request byte for byte with the production code, changing only the one place that holds the filing rule; the
   123	  rebuilt request's archive id must equal the original's, or it is not sent (`resend_filing.py`, AGENTS §5). Never re-send the archive's copy whose
   124	  keys were sorted alphabetically.
   125	- **Articles**: development set = the 54 articles of `selection.json` (already read many times); held-out set = articles the extraction gold read and
   126	  the judgement gold uses that are not among those 54, drawn once before the test, with the list frozen and never changed afterwards. Both sets are
   127	  measured and reported apart.
   128	- **Control**: the unchanged requests re-sent 3 times the same day. No comparison with the archive (model drift).
   129	- **Each answer**: goes through the production code checks and filing first (including "keep only the narrowest" and "no home means dropped"), and is
   130	  counted after.
   131	- **What is counted** (`measure_filing.py`, with its matching rule fixed: items are matched on the distinct numbers and the proper nouns other than
   132	  NVIDIA in the source text; a source passage the system quotes that overlaps the gold's passage also counts as the same matter; "optional" counts as
   133	  optional; the citations in the body of the gold's answers are read):
   134	  - whether each fact that matters (one the gold uses to judge any question) reached the question that uses it, counted per fact, not per "fact ×
   135	    question";
   136	  - per question: the facts that matter that reached it and the new noise that appeared, counted by the decision rule below;
   137	  - the parking lot: how many facts the total-revenue question (v1, together with v22) takes in, and what they are;
   138	  - noise: how many of the sentences the standard does not keep are kept; per question, how noise is filed (links on facts the standard does not keep
   139	    or no question uses);
   140	  - how many core and supporting facts appear; the facts that matter that are dropped; how many questions each fact is filed under on average.
   141	  - Matching still has a small error (spot check: the new rule mismatches a few and misses a few); say so when reporting the numbers, and read the
   142	    ones that matter one by one.
   143	- **Decision rule** (rewritten on 2026-11-04 with Alex's agreement, D360. The original draft required "every draw above the highest of the control's
   144	  three" and the like, which the control itself fails when measured again, so it cannot tell good from bad. Script `decide.py`; written down and frozen
   145	  before each test; each draw's numbers and the totals are all reported):
   146	  - **Totals, with luck ruled out first**: each article's 6 answers from the new and the old arm are randomly reassigned between the two arms 4,000
   147	    times (with a fixed random seed); the new rule's difference counts as a real change only when fewer than 5% of the reassignments reach it.
   148	    - Development set: facts that matter reaching the question that uses them must rise; the count under the total-revenue questions (v1, v22) must
   149	      fall; sentences the standard does not keep must not rise; core facts must not fall.
   150	    - Held-out set: facts that matter reaching the question that uses them must not fall; sentences the standard does not keep must not rise; core
   151	      facts must not fall.
   152	  - **Per question, counted by code against the gold** (development and held-out sets together):
   153	    - A fact that matters which reaches the question at least two fewer times under the new rule than under the control counts as "one fewer" for that
   154	      question; in under the control all three times and under the new rule none of the three, it counts as "lost outright". A move to another question
   155	      that the gold also uses it for and that is no broader than the original (one home per fact, D207) does not count as fewer; a move to a broader
   156	      question counts. "One more" in the opposite direction offsets it.
   157	    - A noise sentence (not kept by the standard, or kept but used by no question) that the new rule files under the question at least twice while the
   158	      control never does counts as "new noise"; filed all three times, it counts as "outright new noise". The opposite direction offsets it.
   159	    - Any question with a net 3 fewer, a net 2 lost outright, a net 5 more new noise, or a net 3 more outright new noise fails. These thresholds are the
   160	      smallest values that keep "misjudged when new and old are exactly the same" within about one in ten; at the test, first compute the
   161	      misjudgement rate from the reassignments; if it is above one in ten, raise the threshold most prone to misjudgement by one step, then compare with
   162	      what was measured.
   163	  - **Smaller changes** (a question 2 fewer, two or three more noise) cannot be told from luck in three measurements: all are listed, given to a reader
   164	    who did not write the rule to read against the raw answers, and written into the report; they do not decide pass or fail.
   165	  Only when everything passes does it become a candidate; a candidate runs end to end three times on the 14-day window (extraction re-sent, matching and
   166	  judging run as usual, scored on the frozen judgement ruler), and that step needs Alex's word.
   167	
   168	## 7. Process (no drift)
   169	
   170	- **One recommendation and one test at a time** (AGENTS §7.3, Alex: "就测试一种，一次"): write the design first and put it through rounds of review (own
   171	  checks, Codex read-only, a reader who did not write it reading the raw records) until a round finds nothing serious; write down and freeze the
   172	  predictions and stop conditions; test once; if it does not match, stop and take it to Alex (D355: "如果有什么不符合hypothesis 的地方你需要终止然后和我说我们重新评估").
   173	- **A review's report is a lead**: each finding counts only once it is checked against the records (AGENTS §1).
   174	- **A prompt audit before any prompt change** (`.claude/skills/prompt-audit/SKILL.md`): check the whole request against the standard sentence by
   175	  sentence, in both directions.
   176	- **Every step goes into `log.md`**: what was done, what came of it, the files; mistakes and overturned results stay in it too.
   177	- **Do not repeat what was ruled out** (§3).

**The work has drifted toward passing checks on one part of the system before establishing whether the whole product is useful.** The clearest way back was already agreed: have Alex review the prepared cards from real system outputs, then use what that review reveals to decide how to compare the systems.

For example, the new system once declined to turn an important matter into a question. A later change recovered all nine attempts on three selected examples, but the test still failed because a separate answer omitted a detail that the unchanged system also omitted. That is a useful finding about the change; it does not tell us whether an analyst gets a better research record. [D656]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS-log.md:9158), [D560]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS-log.md:7056)

### 1. The goal

Alex’s own words describe the goal as a **“hedge fund brain”** that sources information, extracts investment views, links evidence, and maintains a record of events affecting assets and the world. The product design makes that concrete: a continuing, dated record of important investment questions, their possible answers, relevant statements, the current answer and its history, and a final answer when each question is due. A reader should be able to see the reasons and sources. [Product design]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/clean-arch/PRD.md:16)

The filing-phase goal is a necessary part of that: each answer must receive facts that could change it, without piling unrelated facts into one question. The custom-chip example shows why: adding relevant facts already in the records moved the answer out of its lowest range in nine of nine sends; without them, it stayed there in nine of nine. That proves a consequential failure in that example, not that either whole system is better. [Filing goal and evidence]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/prd/10-filing-phase.md:25)

**There is no single numerical finish line for the whole product that Alex has set.** The closest are his six numerical requirements for the step that writes questions and answer choices. The record also has a requirement to beat the old system, but does not define “beats” numerically; the proposed thresholds for using the system on unseen news are not yet Alex’s accepted thresholds. The council, not Alex, put the five replacement checks in their current order. [Product checks]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/clean-arch/PRD.md:126), [D560]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS-log.md:7056)

### 2. Is the work circling?

**Yes, in a specific way:** the team keeps choosing the next task from the nearest failed check, even when that check has not been shown to predict the quality of the final research record. D560 already named “too many local pass-or-fail decisions with no reliable link to what the analyst sees.” It also concluded that both real product defects and the measuring method contribute to the impasse, without establishing how much each contributes. [D560]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS-log.md:7061)

The critique is right about several facts:

- The question-writing check is hard to interpret. In one October reading, the two reader families disagreed on 43 of 244 marks, and further readers disagreed on 41 of 48 disputed points. Those are counts for that reading, not a general error rate for all reviews. [Measurement review]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/reflection-4/codex-measurement.md:18)
- The same older model had seven failures in one draw and one in another. Those draws show why one small test cannot confidently rank models. [Decision index]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS.md:991)
- The new system has not shown that it gives better final answers. In the fresh-week comparison, the old system covered four of five matters both reader families named, versus two for the new system; the support comparison pointed the other way but was affected by disputed controls and small samples. The registered result was **not clear**. [Fresh-week result]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/week/WEEK-RESULT.md:1)
- There is a newly recorded concern about earlier “blind” reviews: Codex readers may have had project memories available. The record does not establish whether any particular judgment was affected, so past results should not simply be discarded. [D661]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS-log.md:9273)

Other claims need qualification:

- **“One to three of 131” describes the earlier luna configuration**, not the later astra result. Astra’s recorded result missed the unjustified-decline requirement by seven; a separate listing point remained disputed. [D645]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS-log.md:8846), [Reflection 8]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/reflection-8/LOG.md:25)
- **D544 was not a claim that the new system had already won.** It was a reversible decision to continue developing it, while keeping the old system running. The reasons included Alex’s rebuild direction and known old-system defects; D544 expressly said it did not establish better answers. [D544]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS-log.md:6616)
- **It was not all checklist work.** The team ran a carried-library diagnostic, traced missing facts, fixed a page that could not display completed new-system replays, and worked on serving data. Whether each was the best next use of effort is a separate question. [D563–D564]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS-log.md:7136), [D609–D610]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS.md:953)
- Decision counts and model changes show activity, but do not by themselves prove waste. Some changes answered Alex’s explicit instructions, including trying Opus and then using astra. [Critique and its count check]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/reflection-9/alex-critique-2026-11-17.md:39), [D646–D648]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS.md:990)

The critique also misses a product risk: **a carried library can preserve a bad question as well as prevent a duplicate.** In the small comparison, an existing combined question absorbed equity-commitment facts, while the empty run opened a separate question. The council corrected the initial positive interpretation: the result fell between its prewritten outcomes. [Stored read and correction]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/carried-library/OWN-READ.md:18)

### 3. Is the scope drifting?

Some work since November 12 directly serves Alex’s goal:

- **Keeping and using a real earlier library** tests whether the system can continue research instead of repeatedly starting from scratch. The two-week diagnostic found no duplicated held questions among six new openings, but was one draw for one company and was not a comparison with the old system. [D563]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS-log.md:7136), [Two-week result]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/carried-run/RESULT.md:1)
- **Tracing facts to answers** addresses the filing goal. The later company-figure investigation found five relevant undelivered statements on three questions, but its second reader did not predict an answer change; that limited result did not justify the proposed effect test. [Decision index, D609–D610]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS.md:953)
- **Fixing the empty product page** served the product review: the writer had omitted records the page needed to display completed replays. The fix was accepted for completed replays, with an unfinished-first-day exception left untested. [D564]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS-log.md:7179)
- **Investigating questions the system cannot answer** is relevant: an important matter that never becomes an answerable question cannot be followed. The drift is treating every local pass as if its effect on the final product were already established. [D559]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS-log.md:6976), [D560]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS-log.md:7061)

Other work moved ahead of the unresolved product question:

- The planner, integration, and live-store slices may eventually be needed to run the product, but their completion cannot decide whether its research is useful. The live-store contract was explicitly for test stores; live operation was not authorized. It was resumed after the final-answer control shortfall rather than after a product comparison established a winner. [D592–D593]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS-log.md:7715), [Integration and live-store decisions]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS.md:937)
- The new final-answer reference is **not an unauthorized alteration of the frozen reference**: Alex explicitly chose to open a separate one, with the old material preserved and his signature required. It addresses a genuine control shortage. But doing it now still advances a component test before resolving the product-level review D560 put first. [D658–D659]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS-log.md:9208), [D560]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS-log.md:7088)

### 4. What was already decided about the way out?

**D559** identified the core problem as turning important matters into questions that can actually be answered and followed. It found that the clean measurements examined had started empty, while the earlier record described a test beginning with a real library. The council did **not** prove that starting with a library would fix the question-writing problem. Alex’s “go” authorized the small comparison; its outcome was mixed. [D559]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS-log.md:6976), [D561–D562]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS-log.md:7105)

**D560** then agreed on this order: first Alex’s small review of actual outputs; then the starting-library comparison; then product work chosen from what those showed. It also reserved a question for Alex after the pilot: whether the six question-writing requirements should remain a mandatory gate or become visible diagnostics alongside a product-level review. Nothing in D560 changed an existing gate. [D560]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS-log.md:7088)

**The deck was built but still waits for Alex.** It contains 16 distinct cards and three hidden repeats, including six real answers from each system, two missed matters and two planted wrong answers. Alex would mark whether each question is worth tracking and whether its answer is supported, with source material available. The deck is a pilot of that review method: its deliberately small and selected sample cannot rank systems, produce a reliable quality percentage, or prove that Alex can replace the other readers. [Deck design]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/pilot-deck-1/DESIGN.md:12), [Deck limits]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/pilot-deck-1/DESIGN.md:64)

The order changed in practice. Alex’s “go” was interpreted as authorization for D559’s comparison while his deck marks still waited. His later instruction to review traces, use the council and execute the next step was interpreted as authorization for the two-week diagnostic. Subsequent work continued on component checks and integration. The record says the deck remained unchanged and waiting; it does not show Alex completed it. [D561]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS-log.md:7105), [D563]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS-log.md:7136), [Current state]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/CURRENT_STATE.md:323)

### 5. The way back: one recommendation and one test

**Stop starting further question-writing tuning, new serving work, and new-reference design rounds until the product review has been read.** Preserve the work and decisions already made. In particular, pausing the reference is a priority recommendation, not a claim that Alex’s authorization has been withdrawn. [D658]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS-log.md:9208)

**First, use the existing [Deck 1]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/pilot-deck-1/deck-1.html).** Ask Alex to mark it as designed, including the three sheets that distinguish a relevant missing fact from one that would change an answer. Then compare his marks, repeats and controls with the stored readers’ marks, retaining their disagreements and the disclosed weakness in past Codex blindness. This costs no model calls; Alex’s time is real work. [Deck design]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/pilot-deck-1/DESIGN.md:49), [D661]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS-log.md:9283)

This test answers the immediate unresolved question: **can this small, source-backed review surface judgments and disagreements that Alex can use to guide a product comparison?** It does not decide which system wins. That distinction matters because the deck’s selection was never designed to rank them. [Deck limits]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/pilot-deck-1/DESIGN.md:64)

Write the result-dependent plan **before** he marks it:

- If Alex can mark it, catches the planted wrong answers, and his repeats are consistent, use his specific disagreements to design the next product comparison; do not declare a winner from these cards.
- If two repeats differ, both wrong answers are accepted, or the deck cannot reasonably be marked in about half an hour, investigate and simplify the review before using it to guide a comparison. Even a perfect pilot does not prove the method reliable. [Deck stopping signals]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/pilot-deck-1/DESIGN.md:64)

The choices that remain for Alex, with my recommendations, are:

1. **Will you mark the existing deck?** Recommend **yes**, because your assessment of the actual research is the missing input. The alternative is to defer it and continue with weaker evidence about what a reader values. [D560]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS-log.md:7088)
2. **After the pilot, should the six question-writing requirements remain mandatory before replacement, or remain visible as diagnostics while a controlled product-level comparison decides readiness?** Recommend deciding *after seeing the pilot*, as D560 specified; the current requirements stay in force until changed. [D560]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS-log.md:7100)
3. **For the next product comparison, should both systems begin with libraries built from real earlier material, with empty starts retained as diagnostics?** Recommend **yes**, while checking the quality of those starting questions and avoiding claims that the library alone fixes the problem. D559’s wider confirmation was not treated as answered by “go”; the council later adopted the real-library condition reversibly. [D561]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS-log.md:7105), [D606]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS.md:950)
4. **What numerical result would be enough to replace the old system?** Recommend setting it only after the pilot exposes what can be judged reliably, and covering important questions, supported answers, and consequential missing facts. The current product design does not define a numerical margin for “beats.” [Product checks]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/clean-arch/PRD.md:126)

**Verdict:** The team has found real defects and made some relevant progress, but it has let a succession of narrow failures determine the work while the central question—whether an analyst gets a better, trustworthy research record—remains unanswered. The next move does not require a new tool or another model run. It is to finish the small product review already prepared, learn what Alex accepts and rejects, and use that evidence to choose the next comparison.
